question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in per-message timestamps to the TUI, and if so should the control be persisted config, a /settings toggle, a slash command, or no core option?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding display/config surface changes TUI UX and user preferences, and the earlier same-repo PR showed that the exact contract matters for rendering, streaming, history, and compatibility.

options.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
options.body: Define the supported control and require an implementation that preserves timestamps across live, pending, streaming, system, and replayed rows.

options.title: Defer to linked PR review
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide whether one of the open fork PRs should be adopted or replaced.

options.title: Decline core display option
options.body: Close the request as not planned and direct users to terminal/logging workflows instead of adding another TUI preference.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
recommendation.body: Define the supported control and require an implementation that preserves timestamps across live, pending, streaming, system, and replayed rows.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent TUI behavior work touched the same ChatLog and history reconciliation paths that would carry this UX contract.
